PB2_MECHANISM_RETRACTED.what_was_claimed: that the only new input stage 2's tracers take is the stage-1 OUTPUT VELOCITY, which is AT-BAR at 2.7e-19, so stage 2 cannot amplify stage 1's one ulp.
PB2_MECHANISM_RETRACTED.why_it_is_false: the reviewer defeated it from the oracle's own source.  At stage 2 Kmm is stage 1's Kaa, so the FCT centred flux built from pt(...,jn,Kmm) (traadv_fct.f90:197-198, 236-242, 265, 273) takes the stage-1 OUTPUT TRACER, which carries the whole stage-1 residual; at stage 1 Kmm == Kbb and that input is bit-identical to the base, so stage 1 cannot see the same defect.  The FCT RHS is also divided by (1+r3t(Kmm)) (traadv_fct.f90:327, 342), a different number at stage 2 than at stage 1, and the qco combine's numerator uses r3t(Kmm) where stage 1 has r3t(Kmm) == r3t(Kbb) (stprk3_stg.f90:677-679).  And nonosc (traadv_fct.f90:316) is a min/max ratio limiter, so one ulp can flip a branch and move an antidiffusive flux by O(1) of its own size.  Stage 2 is NOT a smooth amplifier and the prediction's stated reason was wrong.
PB2_MECHANISM_RETRACTED.the_prediction_itself_is_KEPT_on_a_diffe: stage 3 is still predicted first over bar, now on the size argument alone: 3.1956659540810506e-11 / 3.552713678800501e-15 = 8995, i.e. about 95x per stage, and GYRE at kt=1 starts from rest so each stage operator sits within O(dt*U/dx) of the identity.  A condition number of 95 per stage is not credible for a near-identity operator, so the size demands a NEW TERM rather than amplification.  Everything the reviewer found is exactly the channel by which this prediction can be REFUTED, and it is now named.

PB2_THRESHOLD_COLLAPSED.defect: PB2 carried two thresholds that disagree.  The normalized bar of 1e-15 is 2.346094e-14 K absolute on T (scale 23.460943 K), while PB2 also allowed 'absolute T below 3.6e-14 K'.  A stage-2 T of 3.0e-14 K would pass one clause and fail the other.
PB2_THRESHOLD_COLLAPSED.resolution: the NORMALIZED clause is the threshold; the absolute figure is reported next to it and is not a criterion.  PB2 passes only if stage-2 normalized T and S are both below 1e-15.

PB3_CAVEAT_REGISTERED.defect: kt1.stage3.pre_zdf's oracle side is REBUILT in NumPy from NEMO's records as ((1+r3bb)*Kbb + rDt*(1+r3mm)*after_ldf)/(1+r3aa) (nemo_testcase_l2_gyre_phase3_gate.py:1830-1843). PB6_NEW_the_free_discriminator_the_first.the_record: oracle_qsr_stage3_kt00000001.bin (NEMO_L2_QSR___1), written at stprk3_stg.f90:707-724 around the tra_qsr call at :712.  It carries qsr itself and, separately, ts(:,:,:,jp_tem,Krhs) MINUS a copy taken immediately before the call -- i.e. the ISOLATED qsr-only Krhs increment. PB6_NEW_the_free_discriminator_the_first.why_it_is_worth_a_prediction: tra_qsr is the ONLY operator in stage 3's whole tracer program that touches temperature alone (traqsr.f90 writes jp_tem only).  The measured kt2 residual is T-favoured: absolute T/S = 39.11, normalized T/S = 61.38.
PB6_NEW_the_free_discriminator_the_first.the_sizing_that_makes_it_a_prediction_an: MEASURED from the oracle's own kt=1 entry record over its 18000 wet cells: GYRE's initial T and S are EXACTLY horizontally uniform -- max horizontal spread within every one of the 31 levels is 0.000000e+00 on both -- so at kt=1 all tracer structure is VERTICAL.  The vertical contrast is 19.460410 K on T and 1.718057 psu on S, a ratio of 11.33.  An owner whose error is proportional to the tracer's own vertical contrast therefore predicts an absolute T/S residual ratio of 11.33; the measured ratio is 39.11, which is 3.45x more T-favoured than that.  A T-only owner predicts an infinite ratio.  Neither pure hypothesis fits, so a MIXTURE is the honest reading and this is labelled PLAUSIBLE.
